questions.q: Why are High-Density Lipoproteins (HDL) often referred to as 'good cholesterol'?
options: They transport cholesterol from the liver to the tissues.
They contain the highest percentage of triglycerides.
They scavenge excess cholesterol from tissues and return it to the liver.
They are larger and less dense than LDL.
questions.explain: HDL transports cholesterol via 'reverse cholesterol transport' from peripheral tissues back to the liver for excretion or recycling, reducing the risk of plaque formation.

questions.q: Which of the following fatty acids is considered an Essential Fatty Acid (EFA) that plays a role in reducing inflammation and must be consumed in the diet?
questions.explain: Alpha-linolenic acid (an Omega-3 fatty acid) and Linoleic acid (an Omega-6 fatty acid) are essential because humans lack the enzymes to introduce double bonds before the delta-9 carbon.

questions.q: Which chemical structure characteristic distinguishes a saturated fatty acid from an unsaturated fatty acid?
options: The presence of nitrogen in the chain.
The absence of double bonds between carbon atoms.
The length of the carbon chain.
The presence of a phosphate group.
questions.explain: Saturated fatty acids have carbon chains 'saturated' with hydrogen, meaning they contain only single bonds between carbon atoms ($C-C$). Unsaturated fats contain at least one double bond ($C=C$).
